title: Touring West Virginia coal towns with a show band
summary: Lala describes working in a nine-man band around West Virginia coal mines, earning $75-100 for three nights, refusing to sing, with Ted Weems and Art Weems in the same towns.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: The only thing they got new is they all entertain, they sing and everything, you know what I mean? Yeah. I was working with an orchestra, I swear to God, let me tell you the truth up north. They were traveling around the coal mines in West Virginia, all around these places. And we were only about nine men in the band. Man, that's a good job, coal mine job, man. We'd be in this little town for three nights, man, and make $75, $100, you know what I mean? A snack. Okay. And every man named- But you didn't have a book of them, so? Yeah. A fellow, yeah, a fellow used to book, the fellow that booked us that time, Ted Weems, and his brother Art Weems was working with the Mason Dixon Orchestra, doing the same thing around that time. Ted Weems, Art Weems. Ted Weems booked you? No. He was working the same town sometime with us. Oh, that band. He was working with the Mason Dixon man. Mason Dixon Orchestra he was working with. And we'd make, I mean, that fellow, everyone in that band was a showman, singing this and that. Me, I could, I would sing, I never sang in my life. And I was the highest price man in the band. I wouldn't sing. Every time the piano player would get up to do his song, I had to get on the piano, you know what? But I never sang a song in my life. And all these fellows were all good entertainers. I said no, I never sang a song. Never did, and I ain't gonna start now. And I mean, I had that monkey with me, Santa. Crazy.
